messages.subject: segment function imprecise
parts:
I am working on gecko vocalisations, which are short (~22 ms) pulses of sound. One of the variables I am interested in, is pulse length, and I have used function "segment" to do this (including other things), since "syllables" is one of the outputs. However, when I compare the measurements taken with those I do manually in Audacity, they are almost always longer (using segment), quite inconsistent, and seem to be highly imprecise - I get only 2 different numbers repeated (e.g:
23.21995
23.21995
23.21995
34.82993
34.82993
34.82993
34.82993
23.21995
), for a set of 8 different geckos with considerable variation in their pulse length, which indicates to me that all the variation between those numbers is being ignored. I can't see why that is, as it should be fairly simple when working with a vector of amplitudes to find the start and end of a syllable with a specified minimum amplitude. Any idea what I can do to fix this?

I have attached some sound files, and the code I used:

#############################################################
##Packages:
require(soundgen)
require(seewave)
require(tuneR)

## Set the location of the files to be analysed and make list of the files

file.lst = list.files("[file location here]")

###########################################################################################
##  convert Wav files to Wave objects (TuneR)

waves = lapply(file.lst, function(x){
  readWave(x)
})

###########################################################################################
## filter out frequencies below 0.9 kHz (mostly noise) 
## converting wave to vector

wavesF = lapply(waves, function(x){
  ffilter(x, from = 0, to = 900, bandpass = F, 
          wl = 512, ovlp = 0, 
          output = "matrix")
})

###########################################################################################
## Make spectogram of filtered sound using seewave

spcgrm = lapply(wavesF, function(x){
  spec(x, f = 44100, wl = 512, ovlp = 0, plot =  F)})

###########################################################################################
##  calculates the amplitudes for the frequency-filtered noise

amplts = lapply(wavesF, function(x){
  env(x, f = 44100, msmooth = c(512, 0), norm = T,
      plot = F)
})

##########################################################################################
##  set the syllable threshold value at a standard, normalised to the loudest 2%
#    of the call (rather than normalising to the mean amplitude of the whole sound,
#    which is the default for function "segment" below, and causes too much vairability)

# scaling factor: mean amplitude of top 2%
SF = lapply(amplts, function(x)
{mean(na.omit(tail(sort(x), (nrow(x)/50))))})


# syllable threshold for segmentation ("segment" below), normalising 
# mean amplitude to SF:
ST = lapply(1:(length(file.lst)), function(x){
  SF[[x]]/5/mean(amplts[[x]], na.rm = T)
}) 


###########################################################################################
##  Segment the sound into syllables using normalised threshold value (ST)

seg = lapply(1:(length(file.lst)), function(x){
  segment(wavesF[[x]][,1], samplingRate = 44100, 
          windowLength = (512/44.1), 
          overlap = 0, shortestSyl = 8, 
          sylThres = ST[[x]], shortestPause = 40,
          plot = T, main = file.lst[[x]]
  )})

#median pulse length (milliseconds):
PLmd = lapply(seg, function(x){median(x$syllables$sylLen)})

PLmd #the list of median pulse lengths for each file
